items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: You’ve seen that drum kit Sonny Greer had out there?

ctx.x: Well let me get back to — that was wonderful to hear — I want to get back to you started accompanying visiting American jazz musicians?

Yeah. I got lucky. I was so lucky in fact one of my first jobs, well I went to the university, just to please my parents kind of thing, but I wanted to go, you know, it was three good years. I played with university jazz bands there. And when I left it, I was up at Oxford for three years, and I loved it, that was great. But then I thought now I’ve got to do what I want to do. I’ve satisfied them, you know they made sacrifices for me to go the university, okay, that was nice. And I said I’m going to try and do…

and suddenly you hear this trumpet playing Louis’ signature tune, behind the curtain [scats] “Sleepy Time Down South.” And you suddenly realize here is this guy, coming out, and the curtains parted and there he is. But the magic of hearing that trumpet behind the curtains, before. The sound came before the guy. And you see Louis of course. Just incredible. It’s magical. And I think those kind of guys had that love of entertaining as well, which I think bebop somehow didn’t have. I wouldn’t say they were playing…
